learn.title: Percents in daily life
learn.body: Sales, tax and tips all use percents. The method is always the same: find the percent of the amount, then add it or take it away. We write money in dollars to keep the numbers simple.

learn.title: A 20% discount on 45 dollars
learn.body: The discount is 20% of the price.

learn.title: A shortcut for sales
learn.body: You can do it in one step. Paying 80% of the price after a 20% discount means $0.80\times 45=36$. In general, after a discount of $d\%$ you pay $(100-d)\%$ of the price.

learn.title: Add 8% tax to 50 dollars
learn.body: Tax is an extra percent added on top.

learn.title: Tips
learn.body: A tip is a percent of the bill. A 15% tip on a 40 dollar meal is $0.15\times 40=6$ dollars. A quick way is to take 10% (4 dollars), then add half of that (2 dollars): 6 dollars again.
Discount means pay less, tax and tip mean pay more. Decide which way you are going before you calculate.

questions.prompt: A 60 dollar jacket is 25% off. What is the sale price?
questions.explanation: 25% of 60 is 15, and $60-15=45$. The 15 dollars is the discount, not the price.

questions.prompt: What is the tax on 50 dollars at 8%? Give the number of dollars.
A 40 dollar meal gets a 15% tip. What is the total paid?
questions.explanation: The tip is $0.15\times 40=6$. The total is $40+6=46$.

questions.prompt: After a 20% discount you pay \_\_% of the price.
questions.explanation: You lose 20 out of every 100, so you pay the other 80.

questions.prompt: An 80 dollar item is 20% off. What is the sale price in dollars?
Which is the final price of a 100 dollar item with 10% tax?
A 45 dollar item is 20% off. Put the steps in order.
questions.explanation: Find the discount first, then subtract it from the original price.
